answer: A registry beacon publishes a rotating public challenge that every agent must solve before its trades count; the beacon is anchored to a stake deposit, so a raven-like flood of fresh identities cannot pass for free. Each agent enters the market through a single inlet, a bonded gateway that records its stake and rate-limits new entrants, releasing funds only after a cooling period. Creating a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand deposits, and a sybil swarm that misbehaves loses all of them at once.
